title: 📰 AI news · October 18
takeaway: Keys are in the spotlight again: stored AI-service keys of OpenCode users may have leaked, and a malicious npm package collected keys and passwords from project files. Recommendation: find every place where you saved OpenAI, Anthropic and Google keys, and set a spending limit with each provider.
cta: 🔐 Check where my keys are stored

items.title: OpenCode users' keys may have leaked
items.text: The company behind the OpenCode coding agent reported a breach of its console. Stored OpenAI, Anthropic and Google keys may have leaked for 1.4% of users, and some people see hundreds of dollars in bills for requests they did not make. If you keep AI-service keys in tools like this, check your provider bills and set a spending limit.

items.title: A malicious npm package stole wallets and passwords
items.text: The imgdecode package was downloaded 979 times: it runs hidden code on Windows and takes crypto-wallet phrases, key files and browser data. If you build projects from ready-made packages, your .env files sit in the same places. Check whether imgdecode is among your packages. Free guide "Code protection in one prompt": send the word "защита" to the bot.

items.title: DeepSeek updated its open Flash model
items.text: The model scored 77% on a programming-task test at under 20 cents per task. Weights are open, and the tests are the company's own. For agent projects it is one more low-cost option.

items.title: Claude explained a 25-year-old encryption puzzle
items.text: In 30 minutes Claude showed that the NSA numbers for encryption curves came from a simple random-number generator. The earlier explanation turned out to be wrong. Models are starting to help with old scientific questions.

items.title: At Anthropic agents work 6 times more hours than people
items.text: The share of juniors in technical roles fell from 21% to 14%, and engineers make 5.1 times more commits. The authors note the company is unusually AI-heavy. It shows how teamwork is changing.

items.title: OpenAI plans to build a humanoid robot
items.text: Asked about a humanoid, Altman answered "We will" and expects a demo in 2027. OpenAI's site lists 27 robotics jobs. Looks and price are not yet revealed.

items.title: Honor Win2 gets a 2K 185 Hz display
items.text: Panel maker Visionox called it the world's first 2K 185 Hz screen with 0.93 mm bezels. Honor says the series arrives next week. Some specs come from leaks.

items.title: Data can now be stored in synthetic DNA
items.text: France's Biomemory launched DNA Shield: data is encrypted, written into DNA and kept offline. Suited for copies of encryption keys. Early access for organizations for now.

items.title: Asus released an Intel Arc graphics card for AI at home
items.text: The UGen Arc Pro B70 has 32 GB of video memory, and four cards make 128 GB. It is built for local models. Price and release date are not announced yet.
